title: Project KPI and coverage stewardship

description.need: A project's context map, use cases and KPIs decay quietly: contexts nobody has scanned since the code moved, groups carrying no KPI at all, KPIs with a target and no measurement behind it, and a backlog that is either empty or full of items nobody has looked at in months. None of it announces itself, because each number lives on a different screen and no single reading puts them beside each other.
description.input: The project's context map with the age of each scan, its use cases including the proposed ones, its KPIs with whatever measurements exist, and the current state of its backlog.
description.coreAction: Keep the project's measurement loop honest and moving: read the coverage, decide which gap this cycle is worth closing, populate the backlog with concrete items that carry their evidence, get them executed through the delivery loop, and back-measure so every claim that something improved is a number that moved rather than a description of work done.
description.output: A coverage reading anyone can re-derive, a backlog whose items each name the gap and the evidence behind them, measurements recorded against the KPIs those items claimed to move, and a short note saying what moved this cycle and what did not.

activities.label: Read the coverage: scan age, groups without KPIs, KPIs never measured, backlog state
Decide which gap matters this cycle and which KPI proposals are worth a person's attention
Rescan or propose, and fill the backlog with items that carry their evidence (declare it bound to the context, active only when it has a measurement source)
Hand the items to the delivery loop and follow each one to a result
Record measurements against the KPIs those items claimed to move (env: local for a probe run here, production only for a real reading)
Write the stewardship note: coverage now against last cycle, what moved, what did not

outcomes.statement: The project's coverage is a set of numbers anyone could check, not an impression of how things are going.
successCriteria: Each cycle records the age of the newest scan, the groups with no KPI, the contexts with zero active KPI, and the KPIs never measured
A zero is recorded as a zero rather than left blank, so the next cycle can tell a measured nothing from an unvisited context
The reading is re-derivable from the project's own records without trusting the note that reported it

outcomes.statement: Every gap the numbers name either becomes a backlog item or is written down as declined.
successCriteria: Each item names the gap it closes and the evidence that the gap is real
A gap left alone this cycle carries the reason, so the next cycle does not re-derive the same decision
Items are scoped small enough that the delivery loop can take one on its own

outcomes.statement: No KPI stands with a target behind which nobody has ever put a measurement.
successCriteria: Every active KPI either has a measurement this cycle or is named as unmeasured with the reason
A KPI nothing can measure is retired or rebound rather than left standing as a target
Simulated values stay tagged as simulated and are never reported as observed

outcomes.statement: Every claim that something improved rests on a measurement taken after the work landed.
successCriteria: A completed item's claimed KPI is measured again after the change and the result is recorded against it
A claim with no moved number is reported as unproven rather than as a win
The note compares this cycle's coverage with the last one rather than describing the work done

guidance: Measure before claiming anything moved. Coverage is the first read, usually a wall of zeros: recording the zero is the work. A local reading is recorded with env local and never moves the KPI current value; only production does. Declare the KPI bound to its context before writing any probe; a probe without a declared KPI is homework nobody assigned. Keep technical metrics few and skip what a gate enforces. Proposals go to a person who owns the KPI set; measurements do not, and waiting stalls the loop.

connectorRoles.note: the project whose map, use cases and KPIs are being stewarded

recommendedTrigger.rationale: The loop derives its own cadence from what it reads: a map scanned last week needs nothing, a map six months old needs a rescan before any KPI on it means anything. A fixed schedule would run the same reading whether or not the project had moved, which is how a review turns into ceremony that everyone stops reading.

personalizationNeeds: Which project, and which parts of its map the adopter is willing to have rescanned, since a rescan rewrites rows other people are reading
What this project counts as a KPI worth a person's attention, because a metric that only proves the scan could run is the exact failure this work is calibrated against
How proposals reach a person here, since a KPI proposal is a decision somebody owns and a measurement is not
How stale a scan is allowed to get before a rescan is due, because the cadence of the whole loop is derived from that number rather than from a calendar
Which loop executes the items this one files, so the hand-off is to something real rather than to a backlog nobody reads
dependencies: a delivery loop already adopted somewhere on this project, since this work files items and follows them rather than implementing them itself

examples.title: A registered local checkout as the source_control connector
examples.notes: builtin-codebase's get_contexts and get_context_detail give the map and the age of each scan, which is the whole first half of the coverage read, and create_idea files each gap as an item with its evidence attached rather than as a sentence in a report.

examples.title: The quantities a Personas project already exposes
examples.notes: The Factory surface already carries every number this reading needs: context count, group count, age of the newest scan, use cases with the proposed ones counted separately, active KPIs with proposals counted separately, contexts with zero active KPI, attainment as a percentage, and per-lane freshness reading full, incremental or skip against a fourteen day threshold. A live project pass over one large repository proposed eight technical KPIs and all eight were rejected, which is where the cap on technical metrics and the exclusion of anything a CI gate already enforces come from.

inputSchema.description: The project whose measurement loop this cycle stewards.

inputSchema.name: focus_group
inputSchema.description: Optional context group to read first, by name. Empty = rank the whole map by scan age and unmeasured KPIs and take the worst.
